newsitem.title: USA: China 97/98 wheat imports 10 Mln tonnes - US attache.
newsitem.headline: China 97/98 wheat imports 10 Mln tonnes - US attache.

text.p: China will import "close to" 10 million tonnes of wheat in 1997/98 despite prospects for a large domestic crop, the U.S. agricultural attache in Beijing said in a report released Monday.
Sizable imports will be needed to replenish shrinking stockpiles, the attache said in the report, received by the Agriculture Department last week.
"With low imports and rising demand, stocks are falling, from almost 17.0 MMT (million metric tons) at the start of MY1996/97 to under 10.0 MMT by the end of MY1996/97," the attache wrote.
"Therefore, MY1997/98 imports should be up again and close to 10.0 MMT," the report said. "One cannot rule out the Chinese government continuing to restrict wheat imports for political purposes."

USDA received the report May 14, two days after issuing its first projections of Chinese crop production this year. It suggested a wheat crop of 114 million tonnes and imports of 3.5 million tonnes in 1997/98.
Attache reports are not official USDA data.
The attache report forecast a wheat crop of 110 million tonnes.
It also projected a corn (maize) crop of 110 million tonnes, down about 10 million tonnes from 1996. Corn imports in 1997/98 would be two million tonnes, up sharply.
